data: Every human who has ever lived did so here. The reference orbit by which all others are measured.
The 23.44° axial tilt creates the seasons — not distance from the Sun. Earth is actually closer to the Sun in January than July.
Apollo 8, 10, 11–17 — NASA, 1968–72 (Earthrise; first human views of the full disk from cislunar space)
International Space Station — multinational, 2000– (continuous human presence in LEO)
GOES, Meteosat, Himawari, Elektro-L — geostationary weather constellations
Sentinel 1–6 — ESA Copernicus, 2014– (radar + multi-spectral + ocean altimetry)
Aqua / Terra / MODIS — NASA, 1999–2002– (climate + land + ocean spectroscopy)
DSCOVR / EPIC — NASA / NOAA, 2015– (sunward L1 view; full-disk Earth every two hours)
The astronomical unit IS the Earth-Sun mean distance — Earth is the literal yardstick for every solar-system measurement.
Earth's orbit defines the ecliptic plane. Every other planet's inclination is measured relative to this reference.
Earth's 23.4° tilt is the textbook seasons-machine — equinoxes and solstices arise directly from the angle between rotation axis and orbital plane.
Every Mars launch window — every 26 months — is an Earth-departure Hohmann transfer. The ladder leaves from here.
The Moon is unusually large for its parent — the ratio (diameter ≈ 0.27 of Earth) is the highest in any planet–satellite pair.
Earth's average distance to the Sun, fixed at exactly 149,597,870,700 metres — the natural ruler for solar-system distances.
The plane of Earth's orbit around the Sun — used as the reference for almost every solar-system measurement.
Why Earth has seasons, why Uranus rolled onto its side, and why Venus spins backward.
The cheapest two-burn trip between two coplanar circular orbits — and the baseline mission planners measure everything else against.
Galileo's four-night observation in 1610 ended geocentrism. The system's moons are still ending old assumptions today.
